newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom unit aims for 100,000 users in 97.
newsitem.headline: Telekom unit aims for 100,000 users in 97.

text.p: Malaysian cellular telephone operator Telekom Cellular Sdn Bhd said on Wednesday it hoped to increase its subscriber base to 100,000 by the end of 1997 from 20,000 users currently.

"Our target is to achieve more than 100,000 customers by the end of 1997 and to continue this upward trend until it reaches more than 500,000 by the end of the year 2000," said Wan Muhamad Wan Ibrahim, Telekom Cellular's chief executive officer.
Telekom Cellular is wholly-owned by Telekom Malaysia Bhd.

In December, Telekom Malaysia bought the cellular service for 635 million ringgit from MRCB Telecommunications Sdn Bhd, a unit of Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd. The service was subsequently renamed T.M. Touch.

Telekom Cellular would spend more than one billion ringgit over the next three years to expand its network coverage and capacity, Wan Muhamad said at a function to announce a 211 million ringgit revolving credit facility to finance expansion of the company's cellular network.
The mobile telecommunications industry in Malaysia is currently facing dwindling margins due to the presence of seven major operators providing analogue and digital services.
